# Skill review: audit a skill's quality against best practices

Curated by Skill Harbor — @sanyuan0704's skill for auditing the quality of a Claude Code skill (your own or someone else's): a 3-step workflow under one Iron Law — be specific and actionable, never say "could be improved" without stating exactly what to change and why it matters for model output quality. Step 1, load the target (read the full SKILL.md, inventory every file, count SKILL.md lines — a key metric). Step 2, analyze across five dimensions against the criteria in references/review-criteria.md: structure compliance (standard layout, frontmatter hygiene, no placeholder files), description quality (trigger keywords, no "When to Use" hiding in the body, natural-language matchability), workflow design (trackable checklists, ⚠️ REQUIRED / ⛔ BLOCKING gates, confirmation before destructive ops), token efficiency (Iron Law on top, progressive reference loading, imperative form, scripts executed not loaded), and anti-pattern detection (vague directives, placeholder residue, over-specification, giant monolithic SKILL.md, WHAT-instead-of-HOW instructions). Step 3, report: strengths first (minimum 2, quoted lines), then impact-sorted suggestions each with What / Where / Fix — in a direct, constructive, collegial tone. Honest caveats: a review methodology, not an auto-fixer — it doesn't rewrite the skill for you; and it has its own anti-patterns section, so it judges itself by the same rules it applies. MIT licensed. Skill Harbor never reviews the code, review it yourself before...
